subject: Tiered capacity guardrails & approval matrix for reserved GPU pricing
messages:
From: Leah Davis <ldavis@atlaslabs.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlaslabs.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing and pass-through guardrails for reserved capacity

Hi Alex —

Thanks for last week's demo. Leadership is broadly aligned to move to a Dedicated (reserved) lane, but procurement needs a clearer rubric on how GPU price movements are handled in the contract and what approvals we should expect from Atlas. Specifically:

- We want a banded pricing approach if market GPU spot pricing moves > 20% over the term.
- We need to understand how Redwood will reallocate sku types (A100 vs H100-ish) and whether that triggers pricing re-quote.
- For multi-quarter ramp ups, what guardrails prevent unexpected price shocks to our committed spend?

Can you share a short, actionable framework we can include in our SOW? Also attach any scenario spreadsheet that shows economic outcomes if GPU costs drop 15% / rise 25%.

Appreciate a response this week — Procurement has an internal review on Nov 22.

Best,
Leah Davis
Head of Cloud Ops, Atlas Labs
[attachment: requirements_outline.pdf (pdf, 35KB)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Leah Davis <ldavis@atlaslabs.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlaslabs.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing and pass-through guardrails for reserved capacity

Leah —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short framework and a scenarios workbook (see capacity_scenarios.xlsx) that models three SKU mixes and three market paths (down 15%, flat, up 25%). High level summary below; the spreadsheet has the math and a waterfall you can paste into your SOW.

Summary framework (proposed):
1) Tiered price bands: small movement (<=10%) — no pass-through; medium (10-25%) — shared pass-through (50/50) with monthly reconciliation; large (>25%) — automatic re-pricing trigger with 30-day notice and optional customer opt-out for next quarter.
2) SKU substitution: Redwood will attempt like-for-like capacity. If we shift to a materially different SKU family (e.g., A100 -> H100 variant) because of supply, we treat that as equivalent performance for the purposes of pricing unless performance delta >10%, in which case both parties will receive a re-quote.
3) Ramp guardrails: phased capacity activation (25% / 50% / 100%) over the first 90 days with a price collar protecting Atlas from first-quarter market spikes; any mid-term increases in committed units require 45-day notice and a new pricing attachment.
4) Approval matrix: minor adjustments (<=10% spend delta) — RevOps + Procurement sign-off; medium (10-25%) — Finance + Sales leader sign-off; large (>25%) — Execs (CRO/CFO). See matrix tab in workbook.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in RevOps and Finance for sign-off language (cc'd Marissa and Karthik).
- If you’re good with the approach, we can convert the scenarios tab into an exhibit to attach to the SOW and circulate for legal.

Attached: capacity_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 128KB), redwood_tiered_pricing_playbook.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Tiered capacity guardrails & approval matrix for reserved GPU pricing

Alex —

I reviewed the workbook. A few internal notes for the approval matrix and legal:

- Finance view: shared pass-through for 10-25% swings is reasonable, but we should cap annual pass-through exposure at 15% of contracted ARR unless execs approve otherwise. Add an explicit annual reconciliation clause.
- For SKU substitution, insert an objective perf proxy (p50 latency on 2k token sequence) to determine equivalence; otherwise legal will push back.
- Approval routing: we should add a fast-path for emergency supply-driven re-pricing where the COO or CFO can sign ad-hoc with an emergency notification to the customer and 7-day cooling period.

I recommend we prepare two SOW exhibits: "Conservative" (Atlas gets higher protection: lower pass-through) and "Balanced" (shared pass-through) to let procurement pick. Karthik, what approval language do you need on sales side for the Balanced path?

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
[attachment: finance_memo_short.txt (text, 3KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Leah Davis <ldavis@atlaslabs.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Tiered capacity guardrails & approval matrix for reserved GPU pricing

Leah / team —

Thanks for the patience. Quick note from Sales leadership:

- Balanced path is the default we can offer without exec sign-off: 50/50 shared pass-through between 10-25%, SKU substitution language per Alex's note with perf proxy included.
- Anything that creates >15% ARR exposure or a permanent SKU escalation requires CRO/CFO sign-off. We can pre-authorize a single emergency re-price per 12-month period up to 20% with CFO approval.
- We'll include a short glossary in the SOW that defines "market GPU index" (3rd-party spot composite) and the cadence of reconciliations (monthly).

Action: Alex — can you send the two exhibits (Conservative / Balanced) plus a one-page approval matrix PDF to Leah by EOD Monday? I'll be available for a 30-min readout with procurement if they want it before Nov 22.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
cc: Grace O'Connor (RevOps)
